_doc: Approval-gate (K22) rules for implementing-python-from-spec, read by the plugin's core/gate/spec-approval-gate.py; the file's presence is what gates this skill. Rule IDs carry the skill's prefix because the gate merges every skill's rules by ID. Each setting carries a why; each command rule carries examples that the gate's unit tests execute. A rule whose decision is write decides nothing itself: its writes object names what the matched command writes as a side effect (paths relative to the directory it works in, directory_options, file_options, path_options, operands), and the gate judges that like any other write, so it is denied inside the project before approval.
writable_why: Before approval only the plan, its ledger and planning notes may change. .claude/ holds tooling, not product.
approval_why: The skill asks the user to reply 'approve'. Looser words such as 'ok' or 'go' also answer unrelated questions and would unlock edits by accident.

command_rules.why: A new dependency is a design decision the approved plan names with its version. A package that fails to install may be a hallucinated or squatted name, so it never gets a silent substitute.
command_rules.message: this installs or adds a package. Approve only if the approved plan names it (and this exact version), or you want it anyway.

command_rules.why: A lock file change is a dependency change: it is the approved plan's to describe (which tool regenerates it, and why). uv run and uv sync update the lock on their own unless --locked or --frozen is passed, so the skill uses those flags and asks before anything else rewrites a lock.
command_rules.message: this can rewrite a lock file or remove a dependency. Approve only if the approved plan describes this lock change, or you want it anyway.

command_rules.why: Implementation and verification are local. A deploy, a sync to the cloud or a stack deletion changes a live account, so it is the operator's step, approved explicitly in the session; the skill hands the operator the command instead.
command_rules.message: this deploys, syncs or deletes live resources. Approve only if you intend this change to your AWS account now.

command_rules.why: Implementation and verification are local or read-only. A mutating AWS call from the model changes a shared account outside the pipeline.
command_rules.message: this AWS CLI call can change live resources. Approve only if you intend it.

command_rules.why: python -m venv DIR "creates the target directory" with the environment in it (Python venv documentation). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this creates a virtual environment in the directory it names. Never refresh the project's environment before approval; a missing or broken environment is reported with the setup command from the project's rules.

command_rules.why: Inside a virtual environment pip "will install Python packages into a virtual environment without needing to be told to do so" (Python venv documentation): the environment VIRTUAL_ENV names, or the one whose bin/ holds the pip or python run (.venv/bin/pip, .venv/bin/python -m pip). A virtual environment inside the project is part of it. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. Outside a virtual environment (and with --user, --target, --prefix or --root, which the gate models separately) the install lands outside the project and only the dependency rule asks.
command_rules.message: this pip call installs into or removes from a virtual environment inside the project. Planning installs nothing: name the dependency in the plan, and install it after approval.

command_rules.why: uv pip install, sync and uninstall change the environment VIRTUAL_ENV names, else "a virtual environment at .venv in the current directory, or in the nearest parent directory" (uv documentation, Python environments); --system targets the system interpreter instead. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this uv pip call changes the project's virtual environment. Planning installs nothing: name the dependency in the plan, and install it after approval.

command_rules.why: sam build stores the built artifacts in its build directory (--build-dir, under .aws-sam/ by default) and its cache in .aws-sam/cache (AWS SAM CLI sam build reference). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this sam build writes .aws-sam/ (or the build directory it names) in the project. Build after the plan is approved.
